incident.title: Microsoft 365 / Exchange Online global outage (Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, Copilot, Defender XDR), 12-13 Nov 2026
incident.root_cause: Per Microsoft statements quoted in news (13 Nov): a technical issue introduced during an earlier network capacity upgrade surfaced after a recent network change; many servers became unexpectedly unavailable/unresponsive (a core secure-connection process was overwhelmed), overloading the rest. Not traffic growth, not cyber. Final post-incident report not verified.

status_timeline.summary: Separate Teams incident TM1550488 begins: message sending and chat retrieval failures in North and South America. Microsoft did not link it to the later outage.
TM1550488 Teams incident reported resolved.

status_timeline.original_time: 11:17am US Eastern (3:17am AEDT); The National: 8.17pm UAE time
status_timeline.summary: Start time recorded in Microsoft incident logs (as republished by UPenn) for the Exchange Online disruption, before any public post.
First public post, EX1550543: users in the Americas unable to reach Exchange Online mailboxes via multiple connection methods.
Scope widened: Microsoft 365 connectivity may be affected for users in any region.
Start time of advisory MO1550821 covering Exchange Online, Teams, SharePoint Online, Microsoft 365 Copilot and Defender XDR.

status_timeline.original_time: 1:35 p.m. (ET implied); Suped logs MO1550821 reference at 18:35:36 UTC
status_timeline.summary: Microsoft cites elevated load on part of its infrastructure across multiple regions and starts redistributing connection traffic worldwide.
Microsoft pauses all deployments, moves traffic off affected infrastructure and begins restarting affected servers.
Microsoft says load stems from servers being unexpectedly unavailable, not from extra traffic; reviews recent changes.
No recent change correlates with impact start; failed health checks may originate in a server-health processing component.
Microsoft bypasses the suspect component on a subset of servers and investigates elevated processor usage.
Alternative health-check method returns a subset of servers to service; being applied more broadly; next update 22:30 UTC.
Microsoft keeps restarting servers and weighs reverting a small number of recent configuration changes.
Microsoft admits actions so far have not delivered expected relief; pursuing all pathways.
Microsoft observes limited recovery as users gradually reconnect; traffic shifted to alternate routes.

status_timeline.original_time: 23:06:31 UTC (10.04am AEDT entry in Forbes AU)
status_timeline.summary: Status still service degradation: some servers back and stable, partial recovery limited in some regions; a core process overwhelmed.
Setback: restored servers become unresponsive again once traffic flows through them.
Reintroducing servers a few at a time starts producing positive results.
Microsoft says serviceability changes are not working as expected.
Traffic redirected and partly blocked; partial recovery in some regions but not yet sustained.
Latest traffic-management changes show positive results and are being extended to other regions.
Services start to stabilise; email timeout window extended from 24 to 48 hours so delayed mail is not bounced.
Fix rolling out in stages; Microsoft warns service capacity has not returned to normal.
Recovery proceeding in phases; some infrastructure back online and traffic slowly normalising.
Encouraging progress in Europe; Japan comparatively stable; North America improving; 48-hour timeout kept; backlog prioritised.
US and much of Europe largely recovered; Asia Pacific, including Australia, showing only encouraging signs.
Broader recovery in North America, sustained improvement across Europe, early recovery signals in Asia Pacific; queues near normal.
Recovery spreading; Microsoft apologises for customer impact.
Microsoft reports broad recovery and stability, says it is deeply sorry, promises a full post-incident report.
Cause stated: issue introduced in an earlier network capacity upgrade, surfacing after a recent network change; not cyber or AI-related.
Queued mail still draining; no full-recovery ETA; access may return before mail flow normalises.
Article update says Microsoft has fixed the issues; exact resolution time not given.
UNVERIFIED (aggregator): Lamanna cites gateway defect from July fix, Teams traffic shift, ~14% gateway capacity already down; >80% gateways unresponsive.

claims_check.evidence: No source found giving a cumulative total near 7.4M. Published figures are snapshots: Outlook peak ~128,874-130,000+ (US, ~18:00-18:27Z); Microsoft 365 ~46,000-48,000; Teams ~2,000-4,500; Brazil 7,800; Mexico 4,800. The National cites a peak rate of 19,650 reports/min across five services; Forbes Argentina cites nearly 300,000 cumulative reports (scope unstated). None states 7.4M.

450M is Microsoft's January 2026 paid commercial seat count (HCAMag, citing Office 365 for IT Pros), i.e. the installed base, not seats shown to be affected. Other user-base figures: ~430M (Anderson Economic Group), ~321M (Fox Business). Country reach in sources is 74 countries/territories within an hour (The National; Tom's Guide 'as many as 74'); no source supports 90+.

gaps: Microsoft's own EX1550543/MO1550821 update history could not be read directly (admin center needs login; isdown.app blocked by proxy); timeline rebuilt from news outlets quoting Microsoft, so primary reliability is not assigned.

No verified final resolution time. WindowsForum cites a preliminary post-incident report saying customer impact ended 13 Nov at 11:10 a.m. (timezone unclear) and full recovery 14 Nov; Android Central updated 16 Nov 16:41Z. None verified at source.

Lamanna's three-factor root cause (July gateway fix defect, Teams traffic moved ~15h earlier, ~14% gateway capacity already down, >80% gateways unresponsive) seen only via WindowsForum; IT Pro and BleepingComputer source pages not found.
Per-country Downdetector counts were not found for UK, Ireland, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India, South Africa, UAE, Japan or Europe; only US, Mexico and Brazil have country figures.
No November 2026 coverage found for South Africa.
Irish Independent and Daily Monitor (AFP) pages were blocked (permission not granted): the UK Teams jump at 18:15 UTC and the Washington/Hong Kong decline at 04:50 UTC remain tertiary.

Unverified aggregator claims: IndiGo, Akasa Air, Air India, Malaysia Airlines, Emirates, Bharti Airtel, Richemont, Taiwanese fund managers, Singapore GovTech, Philippines Supreme Court, NZ MFAT, Nelson City Council, Irish HSE Healthmail, Guam DPHSS, Alaska agencies, UK police, University of Iowa Health Care, Unity Health Toronto. Indian airline search hits were the July 2024 CrowdStrike outage.
The 14 Nov phishing warning (AFP via RTHK) and the Hindustan Times/Economic Times full-recovery reports were not found.
AAP originals (InDaily, Newcastle Herald) and ChannelNews failed to load.

Inconsistencies: the Outlook peak is given as 128,874, 'nearly 130,000', 130,000+ and 138,058 (the last via aggregator only). Forbes AU (120k by 17:30Z) and the Irish Times (130k at 17:15-18:00Z) give times before Microsoft's first post. Fox Business puts 'no anticipated relief' at 6:30 p.m. ET, but EFTM quoted it by 22:40Z.
